clue.text: Angered by ban on man's bike

parts.note: angered means cross, as in annoyed
a ban is a bar, a prohibition

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a prohibition on a man riding his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'on' simply join the pieces; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A men's bicycle has a horizontal top tube between saddle and handlebars, which gives the frame its traditional name.

clue.text: Criminal bosses love to appear in hats

indicators.note: appear in means show up inside, so the love letter sits within the hats word

parts.note: caps are hats
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Mafia chiefs like to show up wearing hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear in' puts O inside CAPS; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Capo is the Mafia term for the head of a crime family or a branch of one.

clue.text: Separatist uses Cartesian co-ordinates

indicators.note: co-ordinates read as a verb, arranges, so the letters of Cartesian are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A breakaway rebel uses x and y axes to plot positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'co-ordinates' looks like the noun linked with Descartes, but it is a verb rearranging CARTESIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bigoted for a faction or sect, wanting it kept apart, is sectarian.

clue.text: Tree one trimmed initially to make AA weapon

annotationWithheld.why: Tree one trimmed initially to make AA weapon: BAY + ONE + T (first of trimmed) gives BAYONET, but 'AA' has no job (a bayonet is no anti-aircraft weapon); looks like a garbled 'a weapon', not found online
annotationWithheld.clue: Tree one trimmed initially to make AA weapon

clue.text: Maybe they're private, but non-territorial

parts.note: private here is the lowest army rank, not secret; non-territorial means not reservists of the Territorial Army

explanation.definitionFit: Full-time professional troops, as opposed to part-time reservists, are the standing army.

clue.text: Appeal to recycle paper in church

indicators.note: 'to' here means attached to, so the appeal word is joined on after the paper word

parts.note: to pulp paper is to mash it down for recycling
IT is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A plea for paper recycling is made from the church lectern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' places IT after PULP. The definition works by metonymy: 'the pulpit' stands for the preaching clergy, the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised preaching stand is used figuratively for the clergy or the ministry as a whole.

clue.text: Poet laureate relaxed and happy

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for Poet Laureate
relaxed means eased, loosened

explanation.surface: Britain's official poet is calm and content.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and satisfied, happy with how things are.

clue.text: Proposed to get on, despite being exploited

parts.note: to put up a candidate or idea is to propose it

explanation.surface: Someone suggested getting along with others even though they were being used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' and 'despite being' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone imposed upon, taken advantage of, is a willing victim.

clue.text: New entrant is not here to stay

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A newcomer is only passing through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges ENTRANT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something temporary, passing quickly or staying only briefly.

clue.text: Before day's end, remove feathers from game

indicators.note: 'Before' puts the feather-removing word in front of the letter that follows

parts.note: to pluck a bird is to pull out its feathers

indicators.note: the end of the word day's is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cook is told to dress the game bird before the day is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts PLUCK ahead of Y, the end of 'day's'. 'game' looks like the poultry being plucked, but here it is an adjective meaning brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means brave and willing, the same as spirited or courageous.

clue.text: Beverage and leaf salad at four?

parts.note: greens, or a green salad, are leafy vegetables
afternoon tea is traditionally taken at about four o'clock

explanation.surface: A drink and some lettuce served at four in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain afternoon tea, a light meal, is customarily around four o'clock, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This unfermented leaf infusion, popular in China and Japan, is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Her plans involved gathering shells

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of these two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A woman's complicated plans include collecting seashells on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges HER PLANS; 'gathering' is a link word. 'shells' looks like seashells but means artillery shells.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragments flung out by an exploding artillery projectile are named after their inventor and stand for the bombardment itself.

clue.text: Steals and enters credit-card number

explanation.surface: A thief pockets cards and keys in their numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To swipe is slang for pinching something, and also means passing a card through a reader so its details register.

clue.text: Malign nun touring Ulster

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the nun word goes around the Ulster letters

parts.note: a nun is called Sister
Ulster is used loosely for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A wicked nun is making a trip round Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' signals going round. Ulster, strictly one of Ireland's four provinces, is widely used to mean Northern Ireland, which gives the two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign and the answer both describe something evil or threatening harm.

clue.text: He puts off getting a hanger?

explanation.surface: Someone who postpones things ends up with a garter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting a' links the two senses; the question mark flags the playful second one.
explanation.definitionFit: One who defers or halts something; also a strap that hangs down to hold up stockings or trousers.

clue.text: I'd rejected one girl and another

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters of I'd are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
another girl's name is Anne

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to turning down one girl and then a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' sends 'I'd' backwards, which itself makes a short girl's name, so the answer is literally one girl joined to another.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so it names a single girl.

clue.text: Discover it's an anagram of 2

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the letters of that entry are rearranged

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer at 2 down, the word for separatist

explanation.surface: Find out that this is a rearrangement of another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of the answer at 2 down, the separatist word.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out for certain, establish or determine.

clue.text: Dire pong from small fish

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A dreadful smell rises from a little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pong is British slang for a bad smell, and a dire one is a foul stink.

clue.text: Stretch of river with submerged vessels

indicators.note: submerged means sunk under water, so the vessels go inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A length of river has sunken boats in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with submerged' signals one piece sunk inside another. 'vessels' suggests boats on the river, but here it means cooking pots.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide unbroken area, as of water or land.

clue.text: Top twenty people targeted

explanation.surface: The music chart lists a score of marked victims.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of the most popular songs; also a roster of intended victims.

clue.text: Throw too far because it's dark

explanation.surface: An angler casts too far because it is getting dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'because it's' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcast is to throw beyond the target, and an overcast sky is cloudy and gloomy.

clue.text: Former east German police said to want transport

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken and heard

parts.note: the Stasi was the East German secret police; ex means former

explanation.surface: The old East German secret police want a means of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ex-Stasi, former Stasi, spoken sounds like the answer. 'transport' looks like vehicles but means rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away with joy, an overwhelming delight.

clue.text: New priest displays liveliness

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of priest

explanation.surface: A newly appointed clergyman shows great vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PRIEST; 'displays' links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word means wit and spirited vivacity.

clue.text: Absent-minded dunderhead is characteristic

parts.note: the head of 'dunder' is its first letter
taken as written
a characteristic is a trait

explanation.surface: Being forgetful is typical of a dunce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool, but it is split: the head of 'dunder', its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word describes someone distracted, with their mind elsewhere.

clue.text: Headdress from Croatia rarely seen today

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters lie within the words Croatia rarely

explanation.surface: A Croatian crown is seldom worn nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen today' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular crown worn on the head.

clue.text: Don't take in article — I've got a gift

indicators.note: take in means hold within, so the article letter goes inside the first word

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a is the indefinite article
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A speaker refuses an item, protesting that they already have a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' puts A inside DONT; 'got a' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation or present, especially one given formally, is a donative.

clue.text: Sadly, a monarch returned in state

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the article and the king letter are read in reverse

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Unfortunately, a king came back to his realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns A + K into KA. 'state' looks like a condition, but it is one of the US states.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest US state, in the far northwest of North America.

clue.text: Make further changes to item about poor diet

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of diet are badly arranged

explanation.surface: An editor revises a piece about an inadequate diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' signals a rearrangement of 'diet'; the definition runs to 'item', the piece of writing being revised.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise a text again, correcting a piece of writing a second time.

clue.text: Farewell to Japan

parts.note: read as the word of goodbye spoken in Japanese, not as leaving the country

explanation.definitionFit: It is the Japanese word for goodbye.
